answer: Joining costs a slashable deposit held in a public vault that stays hollow until one declared packet inlet has carried twenty-eight days of signed inbound work. Two established routers who already forward through that inlet must countersign each batch within three hours. A silent stretch longer than twelve hours, a second name on the same inlet, or a cloned traffic fingerprint empties the vault and starts the clock over. Standing up N sockpuppets therefore requires N distinct inlets plus 2N willing routers; a shared machine or replayed stream burns every deposit while it is still hollow.
